candidate_sources.title: Corticium koleroga (thread blight) - CABI Datasheet
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet for Corticium koleroga (Cooke) Höhn. Common names include 'black leaf rot of coffee,' 'black rot,' and 'thread blight of coffee, citrus, and mango.' Covers distribution, hosts (coffee), symptoms, biology and management.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee thread blight (199) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds Fact Sheet (Lucid)
candidate_sources.snippet: Fact sheet on coffee thread blight (also called black rot or koleroga) caused by Corticium koleroga. Describes symptoms — white fungal threads on young stems and tender tissues that turn dark brown, blighted leaves, twigs and berries — plus host range, spread and integrated management including pruning, shade management and copper-based fungicides.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Thread Blight (Corticium koleroga): A Coming Threat for Ethiopian Coffee Production
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed review article on coffee thread blight / black rot / koleroga caused by Corticium koleroga. Discusses pathogen biology, characteristic blight symptoms on leaves, branches, twigs and berries, epidemiology under high humidity and shade, and chemical, cultural and biological control options (Trichoderma, Gliocladium, copper compounds, propiconazole, tebuconazole).

candidate_sources.title: Cercospora Leaf Spot and Berry Blotch of Coffee
candidate_sources.snippet: University of Hawaii CTAHR extension publication (PD-41) covering Cercospora coffeicola on coffee — symptoms on leaves and berries, pathogen biology, and integrated management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Coffee brown-eye spot (142)
candidate_sources.snippet: Pacific Pests & Pathogens fact sheet: caused by Mycosphaerella coffeicola (asexual Cercospora coffeicola). Leaf spots up to 15 mm with light brown/grey centres, dark brown ring, yellow margin; irregular spots on berries causing premature ripening and off-flavours. Favoured by high humidity, warm temperatures, drought stress after flowering; worse under poor nutrition or insufficient shade. Management via shade, nutrition, pruning, and fungicides.

candidate_sources.title: Cercospora coffeicola; Brown eye spot, Berry blotch
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank datasheet on Cercospora coffeicola — covers host range, symptoms (brown eye spot on leaves, berry blotch on fruit), geographic distribution, epidemiology, and management of this coffee pathogen.

candidate_sources.title: Perileucoptera coffeella (coffee leaf miner) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Perileucoptera coffeella (coffee leaf miner) covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Natural Enemies, Impacts, Prevention/Control, and Further Information.

candidate_sources.title: Leucoptera meyricki (coffee leaf miner) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Leucoptera meyricki (coffee leaf miner) covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Hosts/Species Affected, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Natural Enemies, and Further Information.

candidate_sources.title: A Comprehensive Review of the Coffee Leaf Miner Leucoptera coffeella (Lepidoptera: Lyonetiidae)—A Major Pest for the Coffee Crop in Brazil and Others Neotropical Countries
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive peer-reviewed review of the coffee leaf miner Leucoptera coffeella: damage caused by larvae feeding on palisade parenchyma, symptoms including mines progressing from light green to brown, defoliation up to 75%, yield losses up to 87%, and management practices in neotropical producing countries.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Leaf Miner - NKO - Welcome Coffee Growers!
candidate_sources.snippet: Hawaii coffee grower education page dedicated to coffee leaf miner, covering identification, symptoms, and management recommendations for coffee growers.

candidate_sources.title: Ascochyta tarda (leaf blight of coffee) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: A CABI Compendium datasheet on Ascochyta tarda (syn. Phoma tarda) covers Identity, Distribution, Hosts/Species Affected, symptoms, biology and management for leaf blight of coffee.

candidate_sources.title: Ascochyta tarda - Wikipedia
candidate_sources.snippet: Ascochyta tarda (also known as Phoma tarda) is a fungal plant pathogen that causes dieback and leafspot on coffee. First observed in Ethiopia in 1954. Symptoms include leaf lesions, drying of branches, and rotting of flowers and fruits. Pathogen infection favored at 15–20 °C with cold climate, heavy rain, strong wind, and hail.
diseases_mentioned: Ascochyta leaf blight / dieback of coffee

candidate_sources.title: Phoma spot or ascochyta spot of coffee - Cultivar Magazine
candidate_sources.snippet: Phoma/ascochyta spot of coffee: at temperatures below 20 °C, relative humidity below 70% and strong winds, damage is more severe, especially in regions with altitudes above 900 m, even in the absence of rain but with sufficient humidity to cause at least four hours of leaf wetness.

candidate_sources.title: Addressing coffee crop diseases: forecasting Phoma leaf spot with machine learning
candidate_sources.snippet: Phoma leaf spots germinate and infect the photosynthetic area of coffee leaves under optimal temperature and humidity conditions. The fungus Phoma spp. leads to several symptoms detrimental to coffee plants, such as leaf lesions, drying of branches, and rotting of flowers and fruits.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee rust
candidate_sources.snippet: APS Education Center lesson on coffee rust caused by Hemileia vastatrix, covering symptoms (yellowish oily spots on upper leaf surface that expand into orange-yellow powdery rust pustules on the underleaf surface), pathogen biology, disease cycle, and management. Coffee rust is the most economically important coffee disease in the world.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Leaf Rust Hemileia vastatrix Berkley & Broome 1869 (Hawaii Department of Agriculture New Pest Advisory)
candidate_sources.snippet: Hawaii Department of Agriculture New Pest Advisory factsheet on coffee leaf rust caused by Hemileia vastatrix. Includes symptoms (small pale yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with orange urediniospore masses on undersurfaces), pathogen description, hosts, distribution, and recommended management actions for Hawaii coffee growers.

candidate_sources.title: Hemileia vastatrix Berkeley & Broome — CAPS Pest Datasheet (Purdue CERIS)
candidate_sources.snippet: Purdue University CERIS / CAPS pest datasheet on Hemileia vastatrix (coffee leaf rust). Covers synonyms, common names, hosts, symptoms (yellowish oily spots expanding to bright orange/red pustules with yellow border), biology, distribution, pathway, and survey/identification information for the coffee leaf rust pathogen.

candidate_sources.title: The coffee leaf rust pathogen Hemileia vastatrix: one and a half centuries around the tropics
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed review article on Hemileia vastatrix, the basidiomycete fungus causing coffee leaf rust. Describes the pathogen's discovery in 1869 in eastern Africa and Ceylon, its global spread to all coffee-growing regions, life cycle, physiological races, host range (Coffea arabica), and integrated disease management including resistant cultivars and fungicides.
